body: Forward test of the flags-judgment context method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.20 (naive base rate 0.30) that: Indo Tech Transformers' promoter pledge (as % of total shares) is lower in the Mar-2027 disclosure than the 57.93% reported for Sep-2026. Evidence: NSE pledge data (broadcast 20-Nov-2026, SHP 30-Sep-2026): promoter holding 70.29% of 1.062 cr shares; 82.41% of promoter shares encumbered = 57.93% of total. Pledges/encumbrances in favour of trustees (Catalyst Trusteeship, SBICAP Trustee) on behalf of the promoter Shirdi Sai Electricals (SSEL)'s lenders since Oct–Nov 2025; SSEL sold shares on the open market on 29–30 Jun 2026. memdb event:INDOTECH:avoid-2026-11-19 flags this as a red flag. Reasoning: The encumbrance secures the promoter group's own borrowings (not a margin loan), which tends to persist until the group refinances; open-market sales by the promoter suggest liquidity need, not release. Flags-judgment: this flag has a verifiable mechanism (lender security), so we expect it to stay. Resolution: YES if the NSE pledge/encumbrance disclosure for the 31-Mar-2027 shareholding pattern shows promoter shares pledged/encumbered as % of total shares < 57.93% (a fall caused only by the promoter selling pledged shares still counts as YES; any increase or no change = NO). Source: NSE corporate pledge data (tools/nse_fetch.py pledge INDOTECH), SHP for quarter ended 31-Mar-2027. Resolve by 2027-04-30; score with Brier vs base rate.

body: Forward test of the decision-card method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.38 (base rate 0.113, class india_nonfin_1000_20000cr_5y) that: YES if the total-return multiple from 2026-11-23 (entry INR 348.50) to the last close on or before 2031-11-23 is ≤ 0.5, or the stock is delisted/suspended below that level. Model: worksheet scenarios bear 30%→0.38x, base 45%→0.81x, bull 15%→1.58x with σ=0.40; reverse DCF base-case IRR 7.5%; card rule output: size 0: blocked by Expected value vs hurdle (EV 0.89x anchored (raw 0.74x) vs hurdle 1.76x → below hurdle → size 0). Score with Brier vs the base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: India non-financial, mcap Rs 1,000-20,000 cr at T, 5 yrs from 30-Sep-2016 and 30-Sep-2018 (survivorship-free, dead firms included, stratum-weighted). n=208 company-snapshots (54 distress-census D, 153 live L at weight 5.63, 1 delisted-other X at 4.26); 95% CIs (company bootstrap within stratum): P(>=3x) 14.1-28.7%, P(<=0.5x) 7.0-16.1%, P(blow-up) 10.2-21.4%. Two start dates only, and they disagree (2016: >=3x 16%, blow-up 21%; 2018: 26%, 10%). Price return only (no dividends, ~1%/yr). Blow-up = close <=0.2x the close at T, liquidation or compulsory delisting (no fraud field). Remaining survivorship leak toward FEWER failures (IBBI firms renamed/merged and 221 IBBI rows without identifiers missing; voluntary/merger delistings X under-covered). A survivors-only sample from the same frame says P(<=0.5x) 7% instead of 11%.
